works.title: The Tale of Genji — Hakubyō scroll fragment
works.medium: Illustrated hand scroll (hakubyō, monochrome ink line drawing) on paper
works.description: A scene from a later, monochrome ink-line ("hakubyō") illustrated copy of the novel, a distinct tradition from the coloured Tokugawa and Gotoh scrolls also shown here, and evidence of how continuously artists kept reinterpreting Murasaki's novel in new visual styles over the following centuries.

credit.work: The Tale of Genji — Hakubyō scroll fragment
credit.file: File:Hakubyo Genji monogatari emaki - scroll 1-1.jpg
credit.author: Unknown author Unknown author

works.title: The Tale of Genji — "Yadorigi"
works.medium: Illustrated hand scroll (yamato-e), ink and colour on paper
works.description: A later chapter, illustrated in the same early 12th-century scroll tradition, following the generation after Genji's death as his descendants navigate the same web of court rivalry, love and Buddhist renunciation that structures the novel's earlier chapters.

credit.file: File:Genji emaki Yadorigi.JPG
credit.author: Imperial court in Kyoto. The handscroll had been said to be painted by Fujiwara, Takayoshi, though it is now presumed to be painted by several groups of painters in Heian period.

works.title: The Tale of Genji — Hakubyō scroll fragment (II)
works.medium: Illustrated hand scroll (hakubyō, monochrome ink line drawing) on paper
works.description: Another scene from the same monochrome hakubyō scroll, part of a genre of ink-line Genji illustration that favoured clarity of narrative detail over the saturated mineral colour of the earliest surviving scrolls, and was often used as a study or reference copy by later painters.

credit.work: The Tale of Genji — Hakubyō scroll fragment (II)
credit.file: File:Hakubyo Genji monogatari emaki - scroll 1-4.jpg
credit.author: Unknown author Unknown author

works.title: The Tale of Genji — "Suzumushi" (The Bell Cricket)
works.medium: Illustrated hand scroll (yamato-e), ink and colour on paper
works.description: A chapter named for the bell crickets released into a garden Genji has planted to evoke autumn, illustrated with the restrained, geometric interior perspective and stylised wind-blown-away-roof viewpoint characteristic of this earliest surviving Genji scroll tradition.

credit.work: The Tale of Genji — "Suzumushi" (The Bell Cricket)
credit.file: File:GENJI EMAKI -SUZUMUSHI GOTO MUSEUM.jpg

works.title: The Tale of Genji — "Azumaya" (The Eastern Cottage)
works.medium: Illustrated hand scroll (yamato-e), ink and colour on paper
works.description: Part of the novel's final "Uji chapters," set a generation after Genji's death and centred on his descendants' tangled romances, illustrated with the same muted mineral-pigment palette and roofless bird's-eye compositions used throughout the scroll.

credit.work: The Tale of Genji — "Azumaya" (The Eastern Cottage)
credit.file: File:Genji emaki azumaya.jpg
credit.author: Imperial court in Kyoto

artists.name: Jalal al-Din Rumi
artists.country: Khwarazmian Empire (later Seljuk Sultanate of Rum, now Turkey)

works.title: Masnavi-ye Ma'navi (opening)
works.medium: Illustrated manuscript, Persian didactic poem in rhyming couplets
works.description: The opening page of Rumi's six-book masterwork, some 25,000 couplets composed over the last decade or so of his life at the request of his disciple Husam al-Din Chalabi, who wrote down the verses as Rumi recited them, reportedly even while walking through the streets of Konya.

credit.file: File:Opening page of Masnavi of Rumi, Shiraz, circa 1460, Bodleian Library’s Manuscript Elliott 251.jpg
credit.author: 1460 artist, Shiraz

works.title: Masnavi — The Wise Man and the Peacock
works.medium: Illustrated manuscript, Persian didactic poem in rhyming couplets
works.description: One of hundreds of short parables and stories Rumi wove through the Masnavi's six books to illustrate points of Sufi doctrine in accessible, often humorous form, here a peacock plucking out its own beautiful feathers to avoid the suffering its beauty attracts, a lesson on renouncing worldly vanity.

credit.work: Masnavi — The Wise Man and the Peacock
credit.file: File:Illuminated Manuscript, Collection of poems (masnavi), A wise man and a peacock plucking out its feathers not to be attractive to people, Walters Art Museum Ms. W.626, fol. 220b detail.jpg
credit.author: Walters Art Museum Illuminated Manuscripts

works.title: Divan-e Shams-e Tabrizi
works.description: A vast collection of ecstatic lyric poems, tens of thousands of lines, that Rumi composed after meeting the wandering mystic Shams-e Tabrizi in 1244, an encounter that transformed him from a respected legal scholar into a poet, and which he credited by naming the entire collection after his friend and teacher rather than himself.

credit.file: File:A selection of ghazals from the Diwan-i-Shams of Jalal al-Din Rumi (d. 1273) and the diwan of his son Baha al-Din Sultan Walad, Seljuk Anatolia, late 13th - early 14th century.jpg
credit.author: Christies.com

works.title: Fihi Ma Fihi (In It What Is In It)
works.description: A collection of Rumi's informal talks and discourses to his disciples, recorded in prose rather than verse, covering everything from Quranic interpretation to everyday anecdotes, and valued by scholars as the clearest direct record of how Rumi taught and argued outside the formal structure of his poetry.

credit.work: Fihi Ma Fihi (In It What Is In It)
credit.file: File:Fihi ma fihi sample.jpg
credit.author: Rumi

works.title: The Sema (whirling ceremony)
works.medium: Devotional performance: music, poetry recitation and turning dance
works.description: Not a text but a living performance tradition associated with Rumi and formalised by his followers into the Mevlevi Sufi order after his death: a turning dance performed to music and poetry, intended to induce a trance-like focus on the divine. It continues to be performed at his shrine in Konya and by Mevlevi communities worldwide.

credit.file: File:Mevlana Museum, Konya 06.jpg
credit.author: Murat Özsoy 1958

works.title: Matla' al-Anwar (The Rising of Lights)
works.location: Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
works.description: The first of the five long narrative poems making up Khusrau's Khamsa (Quintet), modelled on the Persian poet Nizami's own Khamsa but reworked with Khusrau's own didactic and mystical concerns. This folio illustrates one of its moral parables, a pilgrim humbled by an unexpected lesson in piety from a Hindu holy man.

credit.file: File:"A Muslim Pilgrim Learns a Lesson in Piety from a Brahman", Folio from a Khamsa (Quintet) of Amir Khusrau Dihlavi MET DP120804.jpg
credit.author: Basawan / Muhammad Husayn Kashmiri / Amir Khusrau

works.title: Shirin o Khusrau
works.description: The second poem of the Khamsa, retelling the romance of the Sasanian king Khusrau and the Armenian princess Shirin already told by Nizami, a deliberate act of literary homage and rivalry that was common practice among Persian poets responding to an admired predecessor's Khamsa.

credit.file: File:Amir Khusraw Dihlavi - Khusraw Meets Shirin While Hunting - Walters W62266A - Full Page.jpg
credit.author: Amir Khusrau

works.title: Majnun o Layla
works.description: The third poem of the Khamsa, condensing the widely told Arabian legend of Layla and Majnun, lovers driven apart by their families until Majnun wanders the desert wilderness in grief-mad devotion, into Khusrau's own tightly constructed Persian verse.

credit.file: File:Amir Khusraw Dihlavi - Laylá Visits Majnun in the Wilderness - Walters W624115A - Full Page.jpg
credit.author: Amir Khusrau

works.title: Hasht Bihisht (The Eight Paradises)
works.description: The fourth poem of the Khamsa, following the Sasanian king Bahram Gur as he visits seven princesses, each housed in a differently coloured pavilion and each telling him a story, a structure adapted from Nizami's *Haft Paykar* and often illustrated as a cycle of jewel-toned courtly scenes.

credit.file: File:Bahram Gur and Dilaram.jpg
credit.author: Amir Khusrau

works.title: A'ina-yi Sikandari (The Alexandrine Mirror)
works.location: Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
works.description: The fifth and final poem of the Khamsa, recasting the legendary exploits of Alexander the Great as a philosopher-king, drawing partly on the same Alexander Romance tradition behind Nizami's *Iskandarnama* while adding battles and wonders of Khusrau's own invention.

credit.file: File:"Alexander Fights a Sea Battle", Folio from a Khamsa (Quintet) of Amir Khusrau Dihlavi MET DP120807.jpg
credit.author: Amir Khusrau

works.title: St Francis Renounces His Worldly Goods
works.location: Upper Church, Basilica of San Francesco, Assisi
works.description: One of 28 scenes from the Legend of St Francis in Assisi. The young Francis strips off his clothes and hands them back to his furious father, while the bishop covers him with his cloak. The painting splits into two crowds, family on one side and Church on the other, with an empty gap between them. Scholars still argue over how much of the cycle is Giotto's own work, but its solid figures and clear storytelling point toward the Scrovegni Chapel.

credit.work: St Francis Renounces His Worldly Goods
credit.file: File:Giotto di Bondone - Legend of St Francis - 5. Renunciation of Wordly Goods - WGA09123.jpg
credit.author: Giotto

works.title: Scrovegni Chapel
works.description: The banker Enrico Scrovegni paid for this small chapel, and Giotto covered its whole interior with paint. Rows of scenes tell the lives of Joachim and Anna, the Virgin Mary and Christ, all under a deep blue vault scattered with gold stars. A Last Judgment fills the entrance wall. Below the stories, painted figures of the Virtues and Vices are done in grey to look like stone sculpture. It is the most complete surviving work by Giotto, and one of the great turning points in European art.

credit.file: File:Padova Cappella degli Scrovegni Innen Langhaus West 5.jpg
credit.author: Zairon

works.title: The Kiss of Judas
works.description: Judas wraps Christ in a sweeping yellow cloak as he leans in for the kiss that betrays him. The two faces meet in profile, calm against treacherous, while torches, clubs and lances crowd the sky above. At the left, Peter cuts off a servant's ear. Giotto puts the whole drama into one locked gaze, which makes this one of the most psychologically charged images of the Middle Ages.

credit.file: File:Giotto - Scrovegni - -31- - Kiss of Judas.jpg
credit.author: Giotto

works.title: Lamentation (The Mourning of Christ)
works.description: Mourners gather around the body of Christ. A bare, rocky ridge runs diagonally down the picture and leads the eye to his face, which Mary holds close to her own. Two figures sit with their backs to us, a bold idea that places the viewer inside the circle of grief. Above, angels twist and cry out in the sky. The fresco shows Giotto's gift for turning sacred stories into human feeling.

credit.file: File:Giotto - Scrovegni - -36- - Lamentation (The Mourning of Christ) adj.jpg
credit.author: Giotto

works.title: Ognissanti Madonna
works.medium: Tempera and gold on panel, 325 × 204 cm
works.description: Painted for the church of Ognissanti in Florence, this huge altarpiece shows the Virgin enthroned among saints and angels. Earlier Madonnas, such as Cimabue's, look flat and weightless. Giotto's Virgin has real bulk: her knees push forward under her robe, and her throne recedes like a piece of architecture. It hangs in the Uffizi beside the Madonnas of Cimabue and Duccio, so visitors can see the change for themselves.

credit.file: File:Giotto, 1267 Around-1337 - Maestà - Google Art Project.jpg
credit.author: Giotto

works.title: Giotto's Campanile
works.description: In 1334 Florence appointed Giotto master of works for its cathedral, and he designed this bell tower beside it. He lived to see only the lowest storey built. Andrea Pisano and Francesco Talenti finished the tower in the 1350s, but it still carries his name. Its patterned facing of white, green and pink marble became one of the symbols of the city.

credit.file: File:CampanileGiotto-01.jpg
credit.author: Thermos

works.title: The Ghent Altarpiece (Adoration of the Mystic Lamb)
works.medium: Oil on oak panels, 12 panels (open), 350 × 470 cm
works.description: A huge folding altarpiece. When open, it shows God enthroned between Mary and John the Baptist, Adam and Eve at the far edges, and below them crowds of saints, prophets and pilgrims streaming across a flowering meadow to worship the Lamb of God. An inscription credits Jan's brother Hubert with beginning it and Jan with finishing it in 1432. It may be the most frequently stolen artwork in history. One panel, the *Just Judges*, taken in 1934, has never been found.

credit.work: The Ghent Altarpiece (Adoration of the Mystic Lamb)
credit.file: File:Ghent Altarpiece Google Art Project.jpg
credit.author: Jan van Eyck / Presumably Hubert van Eyck

works.title: Portrait of a Man in a Red Turban
works.description: A sharply lit face turns out of a black background, framed by a red headdress folded in astonishing detail. The original frame carries van Eyck's motto *Als ich can* ("As I can") and the date 21 October 1433. The steady sideways gaze has led many to believe this is a self-portrait, perhaps painted with the help of a mirror.

credit.work: Portrait of a Man in a Red Turban
credit.file: File:Jan van Eyck - Portrait of a Man (Self Portrait?) 1433.jpg
credit.author: Jan van Eyck

works.title: The Arnolfini Portrait
works.description: An Italian merchant, probably Giovanni di Nicolao Arnolfini, stands hand in hand with a woman in a green gown in a room in Bruges. On the back wall, a convex mirror reflects the couple from behind along with two more figures in the doorway. Above it, van Eyck signed in elegant script: "Jan van Eyck was here 1434". Every object is painted with microscopic care: the brass chandelier, the oranges on the windowsill, the little dog. The picture has invited endless theories about marriage, memory and symbolism.

credit.file: File:The Arnolfini portrait (1434).jpg
credit.author: Jan van Eyck

works.title: The Madonna of Chancellor Rolin
works.description: Nicolas Rolin, the powerful chancellor of Burgundy, kneels in prayer across from the Virgin and Child, as an angel lowers a crown onto Mary's head. Behind them, three arches open onto a river valley painted in miniature: a bridge, a city, boats and tiny people, fading into blue distance. That landscape shows van Eyck's mastery of detail at every scale.

credit.file: File:The Virgin with Chancellor Rolin by Jan van Eyck (Louvre).webp
credit.author: Jan van Eyck

works.title: The Madonna with Canon van der Paele
works.description: The elderly canon Joris van der Paele, spectacles in hand, is presented to the Virgin by St George, while St Donatian stands at the left. Van Eyck painted the old man's wrinkled skin, the shining armour and a richly patterned oriental carpet with such precision that they seem almost real enough to touch. The painting is a showcase of what oil paint could do.

credit.work: The Madonna with Canon van der Paele
credit.file: File:Jan van Eyck 069.jpg
credit.author: Jan van Eyck

works.title: Portrait of Margaret van Eyck
works.description: The artist's wife, then 33, looks directly out at us. This is among the earliest European portraits of an artist's spouse. Its original frame records that "my husband Johannes completed me" on 17 June 1439. The painting is plain and unflattering, but warm: it is a record of a real person rather than an ideal.

credit.file: File:Jan van Eyck - Portrait of Margaret van Eyck (1439).jpg
credit.author: Jan van Eyck

works.title: Landscapes of the Four Seasons – Autumn (attributed)
works.medium: Hanging scroll, ink and light colour
works.description: One of a set of four tall scrolls showing the seasons in the monumental style of Chinese landscape painting: towering cliffs, a temple half hidden in trees, houses in a misty valley. Works like this show how carefully Sesshū studied the Chinese masters of the Song and Ming dynasties. He did this before and during his journey to China.

credit.work: Landscapes of the Four Seasons – Autumn (attributed)
credit.file: File:Sesshu Toyo - Landscape of Four Seasons- Fall - Google Art Project.jpg
credit.author: Sesshu Toyo 1420-1506? Details on Google Art Project

works.title: Autumn and Winter Landscapes
works.medium: Pair of hanging scrolls, ink on paper, each 46.4 × 29.4 cm
works.description: Two small scrolls that are among the most admired works of Japanese ink painting. In *Winter*, a single jagged black line plunges down through the sky beside a cliff. It is not really a mountain edge, and it slices the composition in two with startling abstract force. A lone traveller climbs toward a temple through the snow, suggested only by blank paper.

credit.file: File:Autumn and Winter Landscape.jpg
credit.author: Sesshū Tōyō

works.title: Haboku Landscape (Splashed-Ink Landscape)
works.medium: Hanging scroll, ink on paper, 148.6 × 32.7 cm (whole scroll)
works.description: Painted for his disciple Josui Sōen as a certificate of his training, this landscape is made almost entirely of wet, splashed washes of ink. A few quick dark strokes turn the blots into a wine-shop flag, a roof, a boat and two tiny figures. Above it Sesshū wrote a long inscription about his teachers and his trip to China. It is a celebrated example of the spontaneous "broken ink" style.

credit.file: File:Sesshu - Haboku-Sansui.jpg
credit.author: Sesshū Tōyō

works.title: Huike Offering His Arm to Bodhidharma
works.medium: Hanging scroll, ink and light colour on paper, 199.9 × 113.6 cm
works.description: Painted when Sesshū was 76, it shows a Zen legend. The monk Huike, refused as a disciple by Bodhidharma, cuts off his own arm to prove his sincerity. Bodhidharma sits meditating before a cave wall, drawn with a heavy, unbroken outline, unmoved. Huike stands beside him, holding his severed arm. The bold contrast of the simple figure and the swirling rock makes it one of the great images of Zen art.

credit.work: Huike Offering His Arm to Bodhidharma
credit.file: File:Bodhidharma.and.Huike-Sesshu.Toyo.jpg
credit.author: Sesshū Tōyō

works.title: Flowers and Birds of the Four Seasons (attributed)
works.medium: Folding screens, ink and colour on paper
works.description: Pines, plum trees, water and birds stretch across large folding screens, moving through the year from spring to winter. Screens like these, painted in Sesshū's manner, helped make bird-and-flower painting a staple of Japanese interior decoration. It prepared the way for the grand screens of the Kanō school.

credit.work: Flowers and Birds of the Four Seasons (attributed)
credit.file: File:Flowers and Birds of the Four Seasons, attributed to Sesshu Toyo (1420-1506), Muromachi period, 15th century, color on paper, view 3 - Tokyo National Museum - DSC05854.JPG
credit.author: Daderot

works.title: View of Ama-no-Hashidate
works.medium: Hanging scroll, ink and light colour on paper, 89.4 × 169.5 cm
works.description: One of Sesshū's last works and one of the earliest large views of a real Japanese place. The famous pine-covered sandbar of Ama-no-Hashidate stretches across the bay, surrounded by temples, shrines and villages, many labelled with their names. Painted in his eighties, it shows him turning from Chinese models to the scenery of his own country.

credit.file: File:Sesshu - View of Ama-no-Hashidate.jpg
credit.author: Sesshū Tōyō

works.title: Lofty Mount Lu
works.medium: Hanging scroll, ink and light colour on paper, 193.8 × 98.1 cm
works.description: A towering mountain of stacked peaks, waterfalls and pines, with a tiny scholar standing at its foot. Shen Zhou painted it as a 70th-birthday gift for his teacher Chen Kuan. The mountain's grandeur is a tribute to the old man's character. He had never visited Mount Lu. He painted it in the dense, textured manner of the Yuan master Wang Meng, and it is one of his largest and most ambitious works.

credit.file: File:Lofty Mt.Lu by Shen Zhou.jpg
credit.author: Shen Zhou

works.title: Boating on an Autumn River
works.medium: Hanging scroll, ink and colour on paper
works.description: A small boat drifts on a quiet river beneath autumn trees and distant hills, composed in a tall, narrow format that leads the eye upward through the landscape. Scenes of boating, visiting friends and retreat were favourite themes of the Suzhou literati, who valued leisure and friendship above official careers.

credit.file: File:Boating on an Autumn River by Shen Zhou, 1471, Honolulu Museum of Art.jpg
credit.author: Shen Zhou

works.title: Walking with a Staff
works.medium: Hanging scroll, ink on paper, 159.1 × 72.2 cm
works.description: A small scholar with a walking stick pauses among tall, slender trees near a stream and a thatched pavilion, beneath towering, rounded mountains. The dry ink and clean contours follow the Yuan painter Ni Zan, whose austere style Shen Zhou admired but found hard to imitate. Here he makes it fuller and bolder. The figure is often read as a self-portrait of the artist.

credit.file: File:Shen Zhou. Walking with a Staff. National Palace Museum, Taipei.jpg
credit.author: Shen Zhou

works.title: Night Vigil
works.medium: Hanging scroll, ink and light colour on paper, 84.8 × 21.8 cm
works.description: Shen Zhou sits awake in a small house among mountains late at night. Above the painting he wrote a long essay describing how, in the silence, he listened to the sounds of the night: wind, dogs, a distant drum. The experience cleared his mind. Text and image together make this a rare, intimate record of a Chinese painter's inner life.

credit.file: File:沈周-夜坐圖.jpg

works.title: Poet on a Mountaintop
works.medium: Album leaf mounted as a handscroll, ink and light colour on paper, 38.7 × 60.3 cm
works.location: Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art, Kansas City
works.description: A scholar stands alone on a clifftop, gazing across an empty valley veiled in mist. Shen Zhou's poem in the sky imagines the white clouds like a sash around the mountains. The vast empty space, the simple forms and the fusion of painting, poetry and calligraphy make this small album leaf one of the most loved images in Chinese art.

credit.file: File:Poet on a Mountaintop.jpg
credit.author: Shen Zhou (沈周, 1427-1509), Ming Dynasty (1368-1644)

works.title: Crabs
works.medium: Ink and light colour on paper
works.description: Three crabs clamber among reeds at the water's edge, each drawn with a few wet, confident strokes of ink. A short poem in Shen Zhou's hand is written above them. He enjoyed painting everyday subjects such as vegetables, fruit, birds, cats and crabs, which were a favourite autumn delicacy in Suzhou. These quick, humorous sketches show the lively side of an artist better known for grand landscapes.

credit.file: File:Shen Zhou 沈周 - Crabs - y1942-24 - Princeton University Art Museum.jpg
credit.author: Shen Zhou

works.title: The Seven Deadly Sins and the Four Last Things
works.description: A painted tabletop arranged like a giant eye. At its centre, Christ rises from his tomb inside the "pupil" above the Latin warning *Beware, beware, the Lord sees*. Around him, seven scenes of everyday life act out Gluttony, Sloth, Lust, Pride, Anger, Envy and Avarice. Four roundels in the corners show Death, Judgment, Heaven and Hell. Philip II of Spain kept it in his bedroom at the Escorial. Some scholars now credit it to Bosch's workshop or a follower.

credit.work: The Seven Deadly Sins and the Four Last Things
credit.file: File:Hieronymus Bosch- The Seven Deadly Sins and the Four Last Things.JPG
credit.author: Hieronymus Bosch or follower

works.title: The Ship of Fools
works.description: A leaky boat drifts nowhere, crewed by a monk, a nun and a crowd of drunken revellers who sing, gorge and snap at a dangling cake. A tree serves as the mast, and a jester perches in its branches. It is a fragment of a larger triptych, and it mocks human folly and corrupt clergy with the sharp humour of its day.

credit.file: File:Jheronimus Bosch 011.jpg
credit.author: Hieronymus Bosch

works.title: The Temptation of St Anthony
works.medium: Oil on oak panel, triptych, 131.5 × 225 cm (open)
works.location: Museu Nacional de Arte Antiga, Lisbon
works.description: The desert hermit Anthony kneels in prayer while chaos swirls around him: fish that fly like airships, demons in armour, a black mass in a ruined tower, a city burning on the horizon. Bosch invented a whole world of hybrid monsters to show the saint's inner struggle against temptation. The painting inspired later Surrealists.

credit.file: File:Hieronymus Bosch - Triptych of Temptation of St Anthony - WGA2585.jpg
credit.author: Hieronymus Bosch

works.title: The Garden of Earthly Delights
works.medium: Oil on oak panels, triptych, 205.5 × 384.9 cm (open)
works.description: Bosch's most famous and mysterious work. The left panel shows God presenting Eve to Adam in Paradise. The huge centre panel is filled with naked figures frolicking among giant birds, strawberries and crystal fountains. The right panel is a nightmarish, frozen Hell of musical torture instruments and the "Tree-Man". Whether it is a warning against sin or a vision of a lost innocence, scholars still disagree after five centuries.

credit.file: File:The Garden of earthly delights.jpg
credit.author: Hieronymus Bosch

works.title: The Haywain Triptych
works.medium: Oil on panel, triptych, about 135 × 190 cm (open)
works.description: A giant cart of hay, a Flemish symbol of worthless worldly goods, rolls toward Hell pulled by demons. People of every class, from pope and emperor down, grab at the hay or fight and kill each other to get it. On top, a pair of lovers ignore the angel praying beside them. The story reads left to right: from the Fall in Eden to damnation.

credit.file: File:Bosch - Haywain Triptych.jpg
credit.author: Hieronymus Bosch or workshop

works.title: Christ Carrying the Cross
works.description: There is no landscape or sky, only a tight crush of grotesque, jeering faces pressed around the calm, closed-eyed Christ. Saint Veronica, holding the cloth with his image, turns away in the corner. The composition is claustrophobic and almost modern. Its attribution to Bosch himself is debated.

credit.file: File:Kruisdraging, Hieronymus Bosch, ca. 1510, Koninklijk Museum voor Schone Kunsten Gent, 1902-H.jpg
credit.author: Hieronymus Bosch

works.title: Dancing Dervishes (attributed)
works.medium: Opaque watercolour, ink and gold on paper, folio from a Divan of Hafiz
works.location: Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
works.description: Sufi mystics whirl and leap in ecstatic dance in a flowering garden while others look on, some calm, some overcome with emotion. Every figure has a distinct pose and expression. The painting captures the *sama*, the Sufi ceremony of music and movement, with a liveliness that marks the new naturalism of the Herat school.

credit.file: File:Dance of Sufi Dervishes.jpg
credit.author: Kamāl ud-Dīn Behzād

works.title: Timur Granting an Audience at Balkh (attributed)
works.medium: Opaque watercolour, ink and gold on paper, from a *Zafarnama* (Book of Victory)
works.location: John Work Garrett Library, Johns Hopkins University, Baltimore
works.description: From an illustrated history of the conqueror Timur (Tamerlane), made for Sultan Husayn Bayqara. Timur sits enthroned beneath a canopy at his accession in 1370, while courtiers and guards fill a flowering garden in a crowded yet ordered composition. This is one half of a double-page scene attributed to the young Behzād. It shows the courtly world he would record throughout his career.

credit.work: Timur Granting an Audience at Balkh (attributed)
credit.file: File:Timur granting audience on the occasion of his accession (right).jpg
credit.author: Attributed to Bihzād

works.title: The Seduction of Yusuf
works.medium: Opaque watercolour, ink and gold on paper, from a *Bustan* of Sa'di
works.description: Behzād's most famous painting. The story of Yusuf (Joseph) and Zulaikha (Potiphar's wife) is set in a fantastic palace of staircases, doorways and tiled rooms. Zulaikha has led Yusuf through seven locked chambers, but as she reaches for him, the doors fly open and he escapes. The maze-like architecture becomes an image of the soul resisting desire, and the signed work is one of the high points of Persian painting.

credit.file: File:Yusuf fleeing the Advances of Zulaikha.jpg
credit.author: Kamāl ud-Dīn Behzād

works.title: The Construction of the Palace of Khawarnaq
works.medium: Opaque watercolour, ink and gold on paper, from a *Khamsa* of Nizami
works.description: Instead of a royal scene, Behzād painted workers building a palace: labourers carry bricks up ladders, masons lay courses, a man mixes mortar, another hauls water. Each figure is individually observed at a different task. It is one of the most celebrated images of labour in Islamic art, and it shows Behzād's interest in the everyday world.

credit.work: The Construction of the Palace of Khawarnaq
credit.file: File:Kamal-ud-din Bihzad - Construction of the fort of Kharnaq.jpg
credit.author: Kamāl ud-Dīn Behzād

works.title: Alexander Visits the Sage in His Cave
works.medium: Opaque watercolour, ink and gold on paper, from a *Khamsa* of Nizami
works.description: The world conqueror Iskandar (Alexander the Great) dismounts to visit a wise hermit living in a cave in a wild, rocky landscape. It is a lesson in humility before spiritual wisdom. Alexander may be given the features of Behzād's patron, Sultan Husayn Bayqara, and the gnarled trees and rocks show the Herat school's delight in nature.

credit.work: Alexander Visits the Sage in His Cave
credit.file: File:Alexander and the Hermit, from Nizami's Iskandarnama, 1494-95, by Behzad. British Library OR.6810 Folio 273R.jpg
credit.author: c. 1494-1495 artist

works.title: Portrait of Sultan Husayn Mirza Bayqara (after Behzād)
works.medium: Opaque watercolour and ink on paper, album page
works.description: The last great Timurid ruler of Herat, Behzād's patron, sits cross-legged in a plain robe. His face is shown as that of a specific, ageing man rather than an idealised king. The painting is a copy after Behzād's lost original. Such individual portraits were a new development in Persian painting, and they influenced portraiture at the Mughal and Ottoman courts.

credit.work: Portrait of Sultan Husayn Mirza Bayqara (after Behzād)
credit.file: File:Portrait of Sultan Husayn Mirza Bayqara at the age of about 50 years. 1500–25 copy from Behzād's original of about 1490.jpg
credit.author: Kamāl ud-Dīn Behzād

works.title: Annunciation
works.medium: Oil and tempera on panel, 98 × 217 cm
works.description: Probably painted while Leonardo was still in Verrocchio's workshop, this is one of his earliest surviving paintings. The angel Gabriel kneels on a flowering lawn to greet the Virgin. The angel's wings were modelled on a real bird's, and a hazy landscape of trees and mountains opens up behind. There are youthful mistakes in the perspective, but the careful study of nature points to everything that came later.

credit.file: File:Annunciation (Leonardo c. 1472–1476).jpg
credit.author: Leonardo da Vinci

works.title: Virgin of the Rocks
works.medium: Oil on panel (transferred to canvas), 199 × 122 cm
works.description: Mary, the infant Jesus, the infant John the Baptist and an angel sit in a shadowy grotto of strange rock formations and carefully observed plants. Leonardo bound the figures together with glances and gestures in a pyramid shape. He modelled them with soft shadow, the technique later called *sfumato*. A second version, painted after a dispute with the patrons, hangs in the National Gallery, London.

credit.file: File:Leonardo Da Vinci - Vergine delle Rocce (Louvre).jpg
credit.author: Leonardo da Vinci

works.title: Lady with an Ermine
works.description: Cecilia Gallerani, the teenage companion of Ludovico Sforza, Duke of Milan, turns as if someone had just called to her. She holds a sleek white ermine, a pun on her surname and a symbol of the duke. The twisting pose and her long, expressive hand brought a new sense of life and movement to the Italian portrait.

credit.file: File:Lady with an Ermine - Leonardo da Vinci (adjusted levels).jpg
credit.author: Leonardo da Vinci

works.title: Vitruvian Man
works.medium: Pen and ink with wash on paper, 34.4 × 25.5 cm
works.description: A man with arms and legs in two positions fits inside both a circle and a square, illustrating the Roman architect Vitruvius's claim that the ideal human body mirrors the geometry of the universe. Leonardo's notes in mirror-writing record the proportions he measured. Because it is fragile and light-sensitive, the drawing is rarely displayed. Even so, it has become a universal symbol of the union of art and science.

credit.file: File:Da Vinci Vitruve Luc Viatour.jpg
credit.author: Leonardo da Vinci

works.title: The Last Supper
works.medium: Tempera and oil on gesso, pitch and mastic, 460 × 880 cm
works.location: Convent of Santa Maria delle Grazie, Milan
works.description: Painted on the refectory wall of a Milanese convent, it shows the moment Christ announces that one of his disciples will betray him. The apostles recoil in waves of shock and questioning, grouped in threes. All the lines of the architecture lead to Christ's head. Leonardo experimented with painting on dry plaster so that he could work slowly, but the paint began flaking within his lifetime. A 21-year restoration ended in 1999.

credit.file: File:The Last Supper - Leonardo Da Vinci - High Resolution 32x16.jpg
credit.author: Leonardo da Vinci

works.title: Mona Lisa
works.description: Lisa Gherardini, wife of the Florentine silk merchant Francesco del Giocondo, sits before a dreamlike landscape, her smile hovering at the edges of her mouth and eyes. Leonardo kept the portrait for the rest of his life and reworked it for years, blurring its transitions with *sfumato*. Its theft from the Louvre in 1911, and its return two years later, helped make it the most famous painting in the world.

credit.file: File:Mona Lisa.jpg
credit.author: Leonardo da Vinci

works.title: Self-Portrait at the Age of Twenty-Eight
works.description: Dürer faces us head-on, in the symmetrical pose normally used for images of Christ. His hair falls in perfect ringlets, and his hand touches the fur of his coat. The Latin inscription states that he painted himself "in everlasting colours" at age 28. It is a daring claim for the dignity of the artist, whose creative gift was seen as a reflection of God's.

credit.work: Self-Portrait at the Age of Twenty-Eight
credit.file: File:Albrecht Dürer - 1500 self-portrait (High resolution and detail).jpg
credit.author: Albrecht Dürer

works.title: Young Hare
works.medium: Watercolour and bodycolour on paper, 25 × 22.5 cm
works.description: A crouching hare, painted fur by fur, its ears alert and whiskers catching the light. A window is reflected in its eye. Dürer's nature studies were far ahead of their time. This one shows an animal as an individual living creature, not a symbol, and it became one of the most copied images in German art.

credit.file: File:Albrecht Dürer - Hare, 1502 - Google Art Project.jpg
credit.author: Albrecht Dürer

works.title: Adam and Eve
works.location: Impressions in many collections (e.g. National Gallery of Art, Washington)
works.description: Dürer's showpiece of the ideal human body, drawn from classical proportions he had studied in Italy. Adam and Eve stand in a dark forest full of animals, and each animal stands for one of the four medieval "temperaments". A small tablet hanging from a branch carries his proud signature. The engraving's range of tones, from bright skin to velvety black, shows his total command of the burin.

credit.file: File:Albrecht Dürer, Adam and Eve, 1504, Engraving.jpg
credit.author: Albrecht Dürer

works.title: Knight, Death and the Devil
works.location: Impressions in many collections (e.g. National Gallery of Art, Washington)
works.description: An armoured knight rides steadily through a gloomy ravine, ignoring Death, who holds up an hourglass, and a pig-snouted devil lurking behind. It is one of Dürer's three "Master Engravings". It is often read as an image of the Christian who keeps to the path of faith despite fear and temptation.

credit.file: File:Albrecht Dürer, Knight, Death and Devil, 1513, NGA 6637.jpg
credit.author: Albrecht Dürer

works.title: Melencolia I
works.location: Impressions in many collections (e.g. Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York)
works.description: A winged figure sits brooding among scattered tools of measurement and craft: a compass, a polyhedron, a sphere, an hourglass. Behind her hangs a magic square whose rows add up to 34 and whose bottom row contains the year, 1514. It has been called the most debated print ever made. It is often read as a portrait of the creative mind stalled by doubt.

credit.file: File:Albrecht Dürer - Melencolia I - Google Art Project ( AGDdr3EHmNGyA).jpg
credit.author: Albrecht Dürer

works.title: The Rhinoceros
works.location: Impressions in many collections (e.g. National Gallery of Art, Washington)
works.description: In 1515 an Indian rhinoceros arrived in Lisbon, the first seen in Europe since Roman times. Dürer never saw it. He worked from a letter and a sketch, and imagined an animal clad in riveted armour plates with a small extra horn on its back. The print sold in thousands and remained Europe's standard picture of a rhinoceros for about 250 years.

credit.file: File:The Rhinoceros (NGA 1964.8.697) enhanced.png
credit.author: Albrecht Dürer

works.title: Pietà
works.description: Made when Michelangelo was in his early twenties for a French cardinal's tomb, this shows the Virgin cradling the dead Christ across her lap. Her calm, youthful face and the heavy folds of her robe turn the marble into flesh and cloth. It is the only work he ever signed: his name is carved on the sash across Mary's chest. Vasari says he added it after hearing visitors credit the statue to another sculptor.

credit.file: File:Pieta de Michelangelo - Vaticano.jpg
credit.author: original file by Stanislav Traykov

works.title: David
works.description: Carved from a tall, narrow block that other sculptors had abandoned, this giant David is shown before his fight with Goliath, tense, watchful and fully alert. The Florentine Republic set it in front of the Palazzo Vecchio as a symbol of the city's defiance of stronger enemies. It was moved indoors in 1873, and a copy now stands in its original place.

credit.file: File:'David' by Michelangelo Fir JBU004.jpg
credit.author: Jörg Bittner Unna

works.title: Doni Tondo (The Holy Family)
works.medium: Oil and tempera on panel, diameter 120 cm
works.description: Michelangelo's only generally accepted finished panel painting. It was made for the wedding of the merchant Agnolo Doni. Mary, Joseph and the Christ Child twist together in a tight spiral of sculptural bodies and sharp, acid colours. Nude youths lounge in the background. The original carved frame, probably designed by Michelangelo himself, survives.

credit.file: File:Tondo Doni 2015.png
credit.author: Michelangelo

works.title: The Creation of Adam (Sistine Chapel ceiling)
works.medium: Fresco, 280 × 570 cm (part of a ceiling of about 40 × 13 m)
works.description: The best-known scene of the vast Sistine ceiling, which Michelangelo painted largely by himself for Pope Julius II. God, borne on a swirl of angels, reaches toward the languid Adam; their fingers almost, but not quite, touch. Around this and eight other Genesis scenes, he painted prophets, sibyls, ancestors of Christ and 20 muscular nudes, over 300 figures in all.

credit.work: The Creation of Adam (Sistine Chapel ceiling)
credit.file: File:Michelangelo - Creation of Adam (cropped).jpg
credit.author: Michelangelo

works.title: Moses
works.description: The centrepiece of the tomb of Julius II, a project that dragged on for 40 years and that Michelangelo called "the tragedy of the tomb". The seated prophet grips the tablets of the law, his beard flowing like water, his gaze fierce. The horns on his head come from a traditional mistranslation of the Hebrew for "rays of light".

credit.file: File:Michelangelo's Moses (Rome).jpg
credit.author: Livioandronico2013

works.title: The Last Judgment
works.description: More than 20 years after the ceiling, Michelangelo returned to cover the altar wall with a whirling vision of the end of time. A powerful, beardless Christ raises his arm as the saved rise and the damned are dragged down. Its crowds of nudes caused scandal, and after the Council of Trent another painter was hired to add draperies. St Bartholomew holds a flayed skin whose face is thought to be Michelangelo's self-portrait.

credit.file: File:Last Judgement (Michelangelo).jpg
credit.author: Michelangelo

works.title: Şehzade Mosque
works.medium: Cut stone, brick and lead-covered domes
works.description: Built for Suleiman the Magnificent in memory of his son Şehzade Mehmed, who died young, this was Sinan's first major imperial commission after his appointment as chief architect. He later called it his "apprenticeship work," experimenting with a four-semi-dome plan around a central dome that he would refine for the rest of his career. Its twin minarets each carry two balconies.

credit.file: File:Sehzade camisi.jpg
credit.author: Viceskeeni2

works.title: Süleymaniye Mosque
works.medium: Cut stone and brick, with a lead-covered central dome
works.description: The centrepiece of a vast charitable complex built for Suleiman the Magnificent, with hospitals, schools, a soup kitchen, baths and a caravanserai around the mosque itself. Sinan called it his "journeyman work," a step toward surpassing the ancient dome of Hagia Sophia nearby. Sinan and Suleiman are both buried in domed mausoleums in its garden.

credit.file: File:SüleymaniyeMosqueIstanbul (cropped).jpg
credit.author: Hunanuk

works.title: Selimiye Mosque
works.medium: Cut stone and brick, with a lead-covered dome on an octagonal drum
works.description: Built for Selim II in the former Ottoman capital of Edirne, and the building Sinan himself called his masterpiece, completed at about eighty years old. Eight massive piers carry a dome whose diameter finally exceeded that of Hagia Sophia, the target he had chased his whole career, while four slender, fluted minarets frame the courtyard. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

credit.file: File:Selimiye Mosque (15051985908) (cropped).jpg
credit.author: rob Stoeltje from loenen, netherlands

works.title: Rüstem Pasha Mosque
works.medium: Stone construction faced inside with İznik tile
works.description: A small mosque for grand vizier Rüstem Pasha, raised on a shopping arcade above a busy market street, its modest footprint hides an interior sheathed almost floor to ceiling in high-quality İznik tile in the tomato-red that marks the finest production of the period, more densely tiled than any other Ottoman mosque of its size.

credit.file: File:Rustem Pasha Mosque.JPG
credit.author: User:Simm

works.title: Mihrimah Sultan Mosque
works.medium: Cut stone with an unusually large number of windows
works.description: Built at the city's highest point for Mihrimah Sultan, Suleiman the Magnificent's daughter, on a hilltop site that let Sinan surround the single dome with an exceptional number of windows, flooding the prayer hall with light. A popular, likely apocryphal legend reads the light effects at the spring and autumn equinoxes as a tribute to her name, which means "sun and moon."

credit.file: File:Istanbul - Mesquita de Mihrimah.JPG
credit.author: Josep Renalias

works.title: Villa Rotonda
works.medium: Brick and stucco rendered to resemble stone
works.description: A country retreat for a retired papal official, built on a hilltop with views in every direction, and answered with a design of near-perfect symmetry: four identical temple-fronted porticoes, one on each face, around a central domed rotunda. Left unfinished at Palladio's death, it was completed by his pupil Vincenzo Scamozzi and became the most copied private house plan in Western architecture.

credit.file: File:Larotonda2009.JPG
credit.author: Marco Bagarella

works.title: Basilica Palladiana
works.medium: Marble-clad stone arcades wrapped around a medieval brick hall
works.location: Piazza dei Signori, Vicenza, Republic of Venice (Italy)
works.description: Palladio's first major public commission and the building that made his reputation: a new classical skin wrapped around Vicenza's crumbling medieval town hall. His solution, a two-storey arcade of round arches framed by smaller flanking openings, a motif now called the Palladian window, let the load-bearing masonry flex slightly without cracking the stonework. Construction continued for decades after his death.

credit.file: File:Basilica Palladiana (Vicenza) - facade on Piazza dei signori.jpg
credit.author: Didier Descouens

works.title: Teatro Olimpico
works.medium: Wood, stucco and painted trompe-l'oeil scenery over a masonry shell
works.description: Palladio's last design, a covered theatre modelled on his study of ancient Roman precedent, completed after his death by Scamozzi. Behind its stage arch, streets built in forced perspective recede at a scale that makes them appear far longer than the shallow space allows, an illusion still used at the world's oldest surviving indoor theatre in continuous use.

credit.file: File:Interior of Teatro Olimpico (Vicenza) scena .jpg
credit.author: Didier Descouens

works.title: San Giorgio Maggiore
works.medium: Istrian stone facade over a brick basilica plan
works.location: Isola di San Giorgio Maggiore, Venice, Republic of Venice (Italy)
works.description: A monastery church on its own island across the water from St Mark's Square, its bright white facade overlapping two classical temple fronts of different heights to mask the awkward profile of a basilica's tall nave and lower side aisles, a problem Palladio solved more elegantly here than any architect before him.

credit.file: File:San Giorgio Maggiore from the top of St Mark's Campanile.jpg
credit.author: Anton Volnuhin

works.title: Il Redentore
works.medium: Istrian stone facade over a brick and stone basilica
works.description: A votive church commissioned by the Venetian Senate after a plague that killed roughly a third of the city's population, still visited every July in a footbridge-borne procession of thanksgiving. Its luminous white facade and centrally planned interior, lit from hidden windows, are considered among the calmest and most resolved of all his church designs.

credit.file: File:Chiesa del Santissimo Redentore, Venice, Italy.jpg
credit.author: Il_Redentore.jpg : Wknight94 derivative work: Alberto Fernandez Fernandez ( talk )

works.title: Netherlandish Proverbs
works.description: A village packed with people acting out more than 100 sayings, taken literally. A man bangs his head against a brick wall, another fills in the well after the calf has drowned, a woman ties the devil to a pillow. The painting is both a comic encyclopedia of folly and a portrait of a world turned upside down.

credit.file: File:Pieter Brueghel the Elder - The Dutch Proverbs - Google Art Project.jpg
credit.author: Pieter Brueghel the Elder

works.title: Children's Games
works.description: Some 230 children fill a town square with about 80 games: leapfrog, hoops, stilts, blind man's buff, spinning tops, playing at weddings and processions. Seen from above, the crowded scene is a remarkable record of 16th-century play. It may also carry a moral: that adult affairs are just as foolish as a child's games.

credit.file: File:Pieter Bruegel the Elder - Children’s Games - Google Art Project.jpg
credit.author: Pieter Brueghel the Elder

works.title: The Tower of Babel
works.description: A colossal spiralling tower, modelled on Rome's Colosseum, rises above a Flemish harbour city. King Nimrod inspects the work in the foreground while hundreds of tiny labourers haul stone, operate cranes and build scaffolding. But the tower is already leaning, and its lower levels are crumbling before the top is finished: a warning about human pride.

credit.file: File:Pieter Bruegel the Elder - The Tower of Babel (Vienna) - Google Art Project - edited.jpg
credit.author: Pieter Brueghel the Elder

works.title: The Hunters in the Snow
works.description: Three tired hunters and their dogs trudge home over a hill with a single fox to show for their day. Below, villagers skate on frozen ponds under a green-grey sky. It belongs to a series of six paintings of the seasons made for the Antwerp merchant Nicolaes Jonghelinck, and it is one of the most beloved winter scenes in art.

credit.file: File:Pieter Bruegel the Elder - Hunters in the Snow (Winter) - Google Art Project.jpg
credit.author: Pieter Brueghel the Elder

works.title: The Harvesters
works.location: Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
works.description: Another of the seasons series, showing late summer. Peasants scythe and bundle golden wheat while others rest under a pear tree to eat bread, porridge and cheese, one sprawled asleep. The landscape stretches to a hazy bay. It is one of the first great paintings of ordinary working life, with no religious or mythological story attached.

credit.file: File:Pieter Bruegel the Elder- The Harvesters - Google Art Project.jpg
credit.author: Pieter Brueghel the Elder

works.title: The Peasant Wedding
works.description: A wedding feast in a barn: two men carry bowls of porridge on an unhinged door, a piper looks hungrily at the food, a child licks a plate clean. The bride sits beneath a paper crown in front of a green cloth, while the groom's identity is still debated. The painting is full of affectionate, comic detail, and it is one of the reasons for Bruegel's nickname "Peasant Bruegel".

credit.file: File:Pieter Bruegel the Elder - Peasant Wedding - Google Art Project 2.jpg
credit.author: Pieter Brueghel the Elder

works.title: The Chess Game (Portrait of the Artist's Sisters Playing Chess)
works.description: Three of Sofonisba's sisters, Lucia, Minerva and Europa, play chess outdoors while a servant looks on. Lucia glances at us after making a winning move, Minerva raises a hand in protest, and little Europa grins. Chess was a game of intellect, so the painting quietly shows off the family's education, and it brings unusual warmth and spontaneity to a group portrait.

credit.work: The Chess Game (Portrait of the Artist's Sisters Playing Chess)
credit.file: File:The Chess Game (Sofonisba Anguissola) 1555 (4096x3236px).jpg
credit.author: Sofonisba Anguissola

works.title: Self-Portrait at the Easel
works.description: Anguissola paints herself at work on an image of the Virgin and Child, brush in hand, looking straight at the viewer. At a time when women were rarely allowed to train as artists, the self-portrait is a statement of her professional identity. She painted more self-portraits than any other artist between Dürer and Rembrandt.

credit.file: File:Sofonisba Anguissola, Selvportræt ved staffeliet, 1556, Museum Castle in Łańcut.jpg
credit.author: Sofonisba Anguissola

works.title: Amilcare Anguissola with His Children Minerva and Asdrubale
works.description: The artist's father sits with his only son, Asdrubale, and his daughter Minerva in front of a landscape. The boy clutches a small dog, and the relaxed, affectionate poses were unusual for a formal family portrait. Amilcare had championed his daughters' education and sent Sofonisba's work to Michelangelo.

credit.work: Amilcare Anguissola with His Children Minerva and Asdrubale
credit.file: File:Sofonisba Anguissola, Portrætgruppe med kunstnerens fader Amilcare Anguissola og hendes søskende Minerva og Astrubale, ca. 1559, 0001NMK, Nivaagaards Malerisamling.jpg
credit.author: Sofonisba Anguissola

works.title: Bernardino Campi Painting Sofonisba Anguissola
works.description: A double portrait with a twist. Sofonisba shows her teacher Bernardino Campi painting her portrait, but she is the one who painted the whole picture. She made her own likeness larger and brighter than his hand-made version of her. It is a witty meditation on authorship, teaching and who holds the brush.

credit.file: File:Self-portrait with Bernardino Campi by Sofonisba Anguissola.jpg
credit.author: Possibly Sofonisba Anguissola / Possibly Bernardino Campi

works.title: Elisabeth of Valois Holding a Portrait of Philip II
works.description: Anguissola's pupil and friend, the young French-born Queen of Spain, stands in a black gown embroidered with gold, holding a miniature of her husband, Philip II. The costume and jewels are rendered in minute detail, following the formal conventions of the Spanish court. The portrait also carries a personal tenderness born of the two women's years together.

credit.work: Elisabeth of Valois Holding a Portrait of Philip II
credit.file: File:Elizabeth.of.Valois.JPG
credit.author: Sofonisba Anguissola

works.title: Portrait of Philip II of Spain
works.description: The king, in sober black with the Order of the Golden Fleece, holds a rosary. For centuries this portrait was credited to the court painter Alonso Sánchez Coello. Modern research returned it to Anguissola, one of several of her court works that had lost her name.

credit.work: Portrait of Philip II of Spain
credit.file: File:Portrait of Philip II of Spain by Sofonisba Anguissola - 002b.jpg
credit.author: Sofonisba Anguissola

works.title: The Origin of Music, from a Tutinama (Tales of a Parrot) (attributed)
works.medium: Opaque watercolour, ink and gold on paper
works.description: From one of the earliest manuscripts made for the young emperor Akbar, a collection of tales told by a wise parrot. This page, attributed to Basawan, illustrates a story about how music was first discovered. It already shows the lively figures and bright colours that marked the new Mughal style, a blend of Persian and Indian painting.

credit.work: The Origin of Music, from a Tutinama (Tales of a Parrot) (attributed)
credit.file: File:1 Basawan. The Origin of Music Page from a Tutinama Manuscript 1560-65 Cleveland Museum of Art.jpg
credit.author: Basawan

works.title: A European Seated on the Ground (A Drunk European)
works.medium: Ink, opaque watercolour and gold on paper
works.location: National Museum of Asian Art (Freer Gallery), Washington
works.description: A slumped man in European dress sits on the ground with a wine flask, carefully shaded to give him volume. Portuguese traders and Jesuit missionaries had recently arrived at Akbar's court with European prints and paintings. Basawan was among the first Mughal artists to study them closely and absorb their modelling and perspective.

credit.work: A European Seated on the Ground (A Drunk European)
credit.file: File:Basawan. Drunk European seated on ground. ca. 1580-1585. Freer and Sackler Gallery, Washington.jpg
credit.author: Basawan

works.title: Akbar's Adventure with the Elephant Hawai, from the Akbarnama
works.medium: Opaque watercolour and gold on paper (design by Basawan, painted by Chetar Munti)
works.description: One page of a double-page scene from the illustrated history of Akbar's reign. In 1561 the 19-year-old emperor mounted the ferocious elephant Hawai and drove it after another elephant across a bridge of boats on the Jumna at Agra. The boats sink and tilt beneath the animals as attendants leap into the water. Basawan designed the swirling composition, and another artist added the colours.

credit.work: Akbar's Adventure with the Elephant Hawai, from the Akbarnama
credit.file: File:Basawan. Akbar Taming Mad Elephant Hawai. Composition by Basawan, coloring by Chitra. (right part) Akbarnama, ca. 1590, Victoria and Albert Museum, London.. (2).jpg
credit.author: Basawan

works.title: Battle between Rival Groups of Ascetics at Thanesar, from the Akbarnama
works.medium: Opaque watercolour and gold on paper
works.description: In 1567 two rival bands of Hindu ascetics fought over the right to a sacred bathing place at Thanesar. Akbar watched, and let some of his soldiers join the fight. Basawan fills the page with dozens of near-naked, ash-smeared figures wielding swords and bows. Each body is shown in a different pose, with a vigour and anatomical study that were unmatched at the court.

credit.work: Battle between Rival Groups of Ascetics at Thanesar, from the Akbarnama
credit.file: File:Basawan. Battle of rival ascetics. Akbarnama, ca. 1590, V&A Museum.jpg
credit.author: Basawan

works.title: The Vain Dervish Rebuked, from the Baharistan of Jami
works.medium: Opaque watercolour and gold on paper
works.description: From a small, exquisite manuscript of Jami's *Baharistan* ("Spring Garden") made for Akbar's library in Lahore. A proud dervish is taught humility by a wiser Sufi. Basawan sets the scene in a soft, receding landscape with a distant town, showing his mastery of atmospheric depth learned partly from European models.

credit.work: The Vain Dervish Rebuked, from the Baharistan of Jami
credit.file: File:Basawan. The Vain Dervish and the Sufi. Baharistan of Jami. Dated 1595, Bodleian Library, Oxford..jpg
credit.author: Basawan

works.title: Jain Ascetic Walking Along a Riverbank
works.medium: Ink and opaque watercolour on paper
works.description: A lean, white-robed Jain monk walks along a river beneath trees, absorbed in thought, while life goes on around him. It is a late, intimate work, an individual study of a holy man rather than a page of history. It shows the naturalism and sympathy for ordinary people that Basawan passed on to the next generation of Mughal painters, including his son Manohar.

credit.work: Jain Ascetic Walking Along a Riverbank
credit.file: File:Basawan. Jain-Ascetic-Walking-Along-a-Riverbank-ca.1600..jpg
credit.author: Basawan

works.title: Boy with a Basket of Fruit
works.description: Painted soon after Caravaggio arrived in Rome, when he was selling pictures to survive. A young man with bare shoulder and parted lips holds a basket overflowing with grapes, peaches and figs. The fruit is painted with such botanical accuracy that its species can be identified, a sign of the young artist's commitment to painting straight from life.

credit.work: Boy with a Basket of Fruit
credit.file: File:Boy with a Basket of Fruit by Caravaggio.jpg
credit.author: Caravaggio

works.title: Medusa
works.medium: Oil on canvas mounted on a wooden shield, 60 × 55 cm
works.description: Painted on a real parade shield as a gift for the Grand Duke of Tuscany, the Gorgon's severed head screams at the instant of death, blood spurting and snakes still writhing. Caravaggio probably used his own face as the model. The convex surface makes the head seem to jump forward.

credit.file: File:Caravaggio - Medusa - Google Art Project.jpg
credit.author: Caravaggio

works.title: Judith Beheading Holofernes
works.location: Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica (Palazzo Barberini), Rome
works.description: The Jewish heroine Judith saws through the neck of the Assyrian general Holofernes, her face showing both determination and disgust. Her old maid waits eagerly with a sack. Against a black background and a blood-red curtain, the violence is shockingly direct. The picture helped establish Caravaggio's reputation for brutal realism.

credit.file: File:Caravaggio - Giuditta e Oloferne (ca. 1599).jpg
credit.author: Caravaggio

works.title: The Calling of Saint Matthew
works.location: Contarelli Chapel, San Luigi dei Francesi, Rome
works.description: Caravaggio's first public commission, and the painting that made him famous overnight. In a dim tax office, Christ enters from the right and points at Matthew, echoing God's hand in Michelangelo's *Creation of Adam*. A shaft of light cuts across the wall to single him out. Matthew, surrounded by men in modern Roman dress, gestures as if to say, "Who, me?"

credit.file: File:Caravaggio — The Calling of Saint Matthew.jpg
credit.author: Gleb Simonov

works.title: Supper at Emmaus
works.medium: Oil and tempera on canvas, 141 × 196 cm
works.description: Two disciples realise that the stranger they have met on the road is the risen Christ. One pushes back his chair, the other flings his arms wide, and the gesture seems to break through the picture plane into our space. A basket of fruit teeters on the edge of the table, its shadow painted with eye-fooling realism.

credit.file: File:Supper at Emmaus-Caravaggio (1601).jpg
credit.author: Caravaggio

works.title: The Entombment of Christ
works.description: Christ's body is lowered toward a stone slab whose sharp corner seems to project out toward the viewer, as if we stood inside the tomb. The mourners form a falling diagonal, from Mary Cleophas throwing up her arms down to the dead man's hand brushing the stone. Rubens, Géricault, Cézanne and many others made copies of it.

credit.file: File:The Entombment of Christ-Caravaggio (c.1602-3).jpg
credit.author: Caravaggio

works.title: Susanna and the Elders
works.description: Signed and dated when Artemisia was just 17, this is her earliest known painting. Two older men lean over a wall to pressure the bathing Susanna, who twists away in distress. Male painters often treated the story as an excuse for an erotic nude. Artemisia shows it from Susanna's point of view, as an experience of threat and violation.

credit.file: File:Susanna and the Elders (1610), Artemisia Gentileschi.jpg
credit.author: Artemisia Gentileschi

works.title: Judith Slaying Holofernes
works.description: Judith and her maid pin down the Assyrian general and saw through his neck, the blood spraying in arcs across the white sheets. Unlike Caravaggio's hesitant, delicate Judith, Artemisia's women are strong, working together with physical effort. Many viewers read the painting in light of her own trial, though it is first of all a masterpiece of Baroque drama. An earlier version is in Naples.

credit.file: File:Judit decapitando a Holofernes, por Artemisia Gentileschi.jpg
credit.author: Artemisia Gentileschi

works.title: Self-Portrait as Saint Catherine of Alexandria
works.description: Artemisia gives her own features to the early Christian martyr, shown with a palm and the broken spiked wheel on which she was to be tortured. The painting dates from her successful years in Florence. The National Gallery bought it in 2018, only the 21st painting by a woman to enter its collection. It then toured Britain, including a GP surgery and a women's prison.

credit.work: Self-Portrait as Saint Catherine of Alexandria
credit.file: File:Self-Portrait as Saint Catherine of Alexandria (Gentileschi).jpg
credit.author: Artemisia Gentileschi

works.title: Jael and Sisera
works.description: Another Old Testament heroine: Jael raises a hammer to drive a tent peg through the temple of the sleeping enemy general Sisera. Her calm, almost thoughtful face contrasts with the violence to come. The column at the right carries Artemisia's signature and the date.

credit.file: File:Giaele e Sisara (ca.1620) - Artemisia Gentileschi (Museum of Fine Arts, Budapest).jpg
credit.author: Artemisia Gentileschi

works.title: Judith and Her Maidservant
works.description: After the killing: in a tent lit by a single candle, Judith raises her hand to shade the light and listens for danger, sword still in hand, while her maid wraps the general's head in cloth. The suspense, the deep shadows and the glowing gold of Judith's dress make this one of the finest night scenes of the Caravaggesque movement.

credit.file: File:Artemisia Gentileschi Judith Maidservant DIA.jpg
credit.author: Artemisia Gentileschi

works.title: Self-Portrait as the Allegory of Painting (La Pittura)
works.description: Artemisia shows herself as the personification of Painting itself, leaning into the canvas with brush raised, sleeves rolled up, a gold chain with a mask pendant at her neck. A male artist could paint the figure of Painting but could not become her. Artemisia claims both roles at once. Probably painted in London, where she joined her father at the court of Charles I.

credit.work: Self-Portrait as the Allegory of Painting (La Pittura)
credit.file: File:Self-portrait as the Allegory of Painting (La Pittura) - Artemisia Gentileschi.jpg
credit.author: Artemisia Gentileschi

works.title: Old Woman Frying Eggs
works.description: Painted in Seville when Velázquez was about 19, this *bodegón*, a kitchen scene with still life, shows an old woman cooking eggs in a clay dish while a boy brings a melon and a flask. The eggs turning white in the oil, the gleam on a brass mortar and the shadows under a knife are all observed with astonishing precision for so young a painter.

credit.file: File:Diego Velazquez - An Old Woman Cooking Eggs - Google Art Project.jpg
credit.author: Diego Velázquez

works.title: The Waterseller of Seville
works.description: A dignified old water-seller hands a glass to a boy, while a man drinks in the shadows behind. A fig floats in the glass to freshen the water, and drops bead on the great clay jug. Velázquez gives a street vendor the gravity of a saint. The painting was captured from Joseph Bonaparte's baggage after the Battle of Vitoria in 1813 and given to the Duke of Wellington.

credit.file: File:El aguador de Sevilla, por Diego Velázquez.jpg
credit.author: Diego Velázquez

works.title: The Surrender of Breda
works.description: Painted for the Hall of Realms in the Buen Retiro Palace, it commemorates a Spanish victory of 1625 in the war with the Dutch. Instead of triumph, Velázquez shows courtesy: the Spanish general Ambrogio Spinola lays a consoling hand on the shoulder of the defeated Justinus of Nassau as he hands over the city's keys. Behind the Spanish, a forest of upright lances gave the painting its popular name, *Las Lanzas*.

credit.file: File:Velazquez-The Surrender of Breda.jpg
credit.author: Diego Velázquez

works.title: The Rokeby Venus (The Toilet of Venus)
works.description: The only surviving female nude by Velázquez, a rare subject in Catholic Spain. Venus reclines with her back to us, gazing into a mirror held by Cupid, where her face appears as a soft blur. In 1914 the suffragette Mary Richardson slashed the canvas with a meat cleaver in protest at the arrest of Emmeline Pankhurst. It was skilfully restored.

credit.work: The Rokeby Venus (The Toilet of Venus)
credit.file: File:Diego Velázquez - Rokeby Venus.jpg
credit.author: Diego Velázquez

works.title: Portrait of Pope Innocent X
works.description: Painted during Velázquez's second trip to Italy, this portrait shows the 75-year-old pope in shimmering red and white, his sharp, suspicious gaze fixed on the viewer. Innocent is said to have remarked that it was *troppo vero*, "too true". Three centuries later it obsessed Francis Bacon, who painted dozens of screaming variations on it.

credit.file: File:Retrato del Papa Inocencio X. Roma, by Diego Velázquez.jpg
credit.author: Diego Velázquez

works.title: Las Meninas
works.description: The little Infanta Margarita stands among her maids of honour, a dwarf, a dog and courtiers. At the left Velázquez himself stands at a vast canvas, brush poised. In a mirror on the back wall appear the king and queen, standing, it seems, exactly where we stand. Who is looking at whom? The picture's puzzles about seeing and representation have made it perhaps the most analysed painting in Western art.

credit.file: File:Las Meninas, by Diego Velázquez, from Prado in Google Earth.jpg
credit.author: Diego Velázquez

works.title: The Anatomy Lesson of Dr Nicolaes Tulp
works.description: Rembrandt's first big commission in Amsterdam, painted at 26. The city's leading anatomist demonstrates the muscles of a dissected arm to seven surgeons, who lean in with varied expressions of attention. Group portraits were usually stiff rows of heads. Rembrandt turned this one into a dramatic scene of learning, and it made his name.

credit.work: The Anatomy Lesson of Dr Nicolaes Tulp
credit.file: File:Rembrandt - The Anatomy Lesson of Dr Nicolaes Tulp.jpg
credit.author: Rembrandt

works.title: The Night Watch (Militia Company of District II under Captain Frans Banninck Cocq)
works.description: A company of civic guardsmen bursts into motion as their captain gives the order to march. Muskets are loaded, a drum beats, a dog barks, and a glowing girl carries the company's emblem, a chicken's claw. It is not a night scene: the name came from darkened varnish, removed in later restorations. Since 2019 the Rijksmuseum has studied and restored it in public, in a glass room.

credit.work: The Night Watch (Militia Company of District II under Captain Frans Banninck Cocq)
credit.file: File:La ronda de noche, por Rembrandt van Rijn.jpg
credit.author: Rembrandt

works.title: The Hundred Guilder Print (Christ Healing the Sick)
works.location: Impressions in many collections (e.g. Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam)
works.description: Rembrandt's most ambitious print gathers several episodes from Matthew 19 around a radiant Christ: the sick being brought to him, mothers with children, arguing Pharisees and a rich young man. It is densely worked in dark shadows on the left and left almost bare on the right. Its nickname comes from the very high price it was said to fetch.

credit.work: The Hundred Guilder Print (Christ Healing the Sick)
credit.file: File:Rembrandt The Hundred Guilder Print.jpg
credit.author: Rembrandt

works.title: Self-Portrait with Two Circles
works.description: One of the last and greatest of Rembrandt's roughly 80 self-portraits. The ageing, bankrupt artist stands before us with palette and brushes, in a plain fur-lined robe and white cap, looking straight out. Two mysterious arcs on the wall behind have been read as symbols of perfection, a map of the world, or a display of the painter's skill.

credit.file: File:Rembrandt Self-portrait (Kenwood).jpg
credit.author: Rembrandt

works.title: The Jewish Bride
works.description: A couple, probably portrayed as the biblical Isaac and Rebecca, stand in a tender embrace, his hand resting on her breast, hers touching his. The sleeves are built up with thick paint applied with a palette knife, glowing gold and red. Vincent van Gogh said he would give ten years of his life to sit in front of it for a fortnight with only a crust of bread.

credit.file: File:Rembrandt Harmensz. van Rijn - Portret van een paar als oudtestamentische figuren, genaamd 'Het Joodse bruidje' - Google Art Project.jpg
credit.author: Rembrandt

works.title: The Return of the Prodigal Son
works.description: The ragged son kneels, shaven-headed and barefoot, pressing his face against his old father's chest. The father rests both hands on his back in forgiveness, while the elder brother watches coldly from the right. Painted near the end of Rembrandt's life, it is one of the most moving images of mercy in art.

credit.work: The Return of the Prodigal Son
credit.file: File:Rembrandt Harmensz van Rijn - Return of the Prodigal Son - Google Art Project.jpg
credit.author: Rembrandt

works.title: St Paul's Cathedral
works.medium: Portland stone, with a triple-shell lead-covered dome
works.location: Ludgate Hill, City of London, England
works.description: Wren's masterpiece and the building he spent 35 years on, rising on the site of a medieval cathedral gutted in the Great Fire of London. Its dome is really three shells in one: a shallow inner dome seen from the floor, a hidden brick cone that carries the real structural load, and a tall outer dome of timber and lead that gives St Paul's its skyline silhouette. Wren's son laid the final stone in 1710.

credit.file: File:St Pauls aerial (cropped).jpg
credit.author: Mark Fosh

works.title: Royal Observatory, Greenwich
works.medium: Brick with stone dressings, built partly from recycled materials from a demolished fort
works.description: Built in under a year for the newly created post of Astronomer Royal, John Flamsteed, on the foundations of an old fort in Greenwich Park. Wren, himself a former professor of astronomy, oriented the main hall along a north-south meridian; the site later gave its name to Greenwich Mean Time and the line of zero longitude.

credit.file: File:Royal observatory greenwich.jpg

works.title: Royal Hospital Chelsea
works.medium: Brick with stone dressings around three courtyards
works.description: A retirement and nursing home for army veterans, commissioned by Charles II and modelled loosely on Les Invalides in Paris, arranged around three plain, dignified brick courtyards rather than a single showpiece facade. It still houses several hundred retired soldiers, known as Chelsea Pensioners, who continue to wear the scarlet coats introduced in Wren's time.

credit.file: File:The Royal Hospital Chelsea (1).jpg
credit.author: Colin McLaughlin

works.title: St Stephen Walbrook
works.medium: Stone piers and a coffered dome on a wooden frame
works.description: One of more than fifty City parish churches Wren rebuilt after the Great Fire, squeezed onto an awkward, irregular plot yet crowned with a coffered dome carried on slender Corinthian columns, widely read as his working study for the dome of St Paul's, then still on the drawing board a few streets away.

credit.file: File:St Stephen Walbrook 20130324 033.jpg
credit.author: Elisa.rolle

works.title: The Monument to the Great Fire of London
works.medium: Portland stone Doric column with an internal spiral staircase
works.location: Monument Street, City of London, England
works.description: A fluted Doric column raised, with Robert Hooke, near the bakery where the Great Fire of 1666 began, its height of 202 feet equal to its exact distance from the fire's starting point. A gilded urn of flames tops the column, and 311 steps of an internal spiral staircase lead to a viewing platform still open to the public.

credit.work: The Monument to the Great Fire of London
credit.file: File:The Monument to the Great Fire of London.JPG
credit.author: Eluveitie

works.title: The Milkmaid
works.description: A sturdy kitchen maid pours a thin stream of milk into an earthenware bowl, utterly absorbed in her work. Light from the window picks out the crusty bread in dots of paint, the nail holes in the plaster wall, and the ultramarine of her apron. Vermeer makes a simple household task feel timeless and quietly heroic.

credit.file: File:Johannes Vermeer - Het melkmeisje - Google Art Project.png
credit.author: Johannes Vermeer

works.title: The Little Street
works.description: A view of ordinary brick houses in Delft, with a woman sewing in a doorway, another busy in an alleyway, and children playing on the pavement. Every crack and patch of whitewash is lovingly recorded. In 2015 archival research identified the exact site, on the Vlamingstraat, where Vermeer's aunt lived.

credit.file: File:Johannes Vermeer - Gezicht op huizen in Delft, bekend als 'Het straatje' - Google Art Project.jpg
credit.author: Johannes Vermeer

works.title: View of Delft
works.description: Vermeer's hometown seen across the water on a morning after rain, under towering clouds. Parts of the city lie in shadow while sunlight strikes a distant church tower and rooftops. He mixed sand into some of his paint to catch the texture of brick and stone. In Proust's *In Search of Lost Time*, the writer Bergotte dies gazing at its "little patch of yellow wall".

credit.file: File:Vermeer-view-of-delft.jpg
credit.author: Johannes Vermeer

works.title: Woman Holding a Balance
works.description: A woman in a fur-trimmed jacket stands at a table strewn with pearls and gold, holding a small, empty balance up to the soft window light. On the wall behind her hangs a painting of the Last Judgment, when souls are weighed. The picture is a meditation on balance, temperance and the choices of daily life.

credit.file: File:Johannes Vermeer - Woman Holding a Balance - Google Art Project.jpg
credit.author: Johannes Vermeer

works.title: Girl with a Pearl Earring
works.description: Not a portrait but a *tronie*, a study of a character or type. A girl in an exotic blue and yellow turban turns over her shoulder toward us, lips parted, a large pearl gleaming at her ear. The pearl is just two strokes of paint. Often called the "Mona Lisa of the North", it inspired a best-selling novel and a 2003 film.

credit.file: File:1665 Girl with a Pearl Earring.jpg
credit.author: Johannes Vermeer

works.title: The Art of Painting
works.description: A heavy tapestry is drawn back to reveal a painter, seen from behind, painting a model dressed as Clio, the muse of history, with a trumpet and a book. A large map of the Netherlands covers the back wall. Vermeer kept this allegory of his art until his death. In 1940 it was bought by Adolf Hitler; after the war it went to Vienna, and restitution claims for it were rejected in 2011.

credit.file: File:Jan Vermeer - The Art of Painting - Google Art Project.jpg
credit.author: Johannes Vermeer

works.title: General View of Mount Geumgang (Geumgang jeondo)
works.medium: Hanging scroll, ink and light colour on paper, 130.7 × 94.1 cm
works.location: Leeum, Samsung Museum of Art, Seoul (National Treasure)
works.description: The famous Diamond Mountains of Korea's east coast seen as if from the air, packed into a great circular composition. Sharp white granite peaks, drawn with vertical, needle-like strokes, rise around softer, wooded earthen hills rendered with wet dots. Jeong Seon balanced them like the yin and yang of Korean thought. It is one of the landmark images of Korean art.

credit.work: General View of Mount Geumgang (Geumgang jeondo)
credit.file: File:Geumgangjeondo.jpg
credit.author: Jeong Seon

works.title: Valley of Clear Wind (Cheongpunggye)
works.medium: Hanging scroll, ink and light colour on silk
works.description: A wooded valley at the foot of Mount Inwang in Seoul, where a scholarly family kept a pavilion among pines and rocks. Jeong Seon painted many such views of real places in and around the capital. He mixed dense, dark ink with lighter washes to capture the texture of the hills he knew from daily walks.

credit.file: File:Jeong Seon-Cheongpung.gye-02.jpg
credit.author: Jeong Seon

works.title: Overview of Inner Mount Geumgang in Autumn (Pungak naesan chongram)
works.medium: Hanging scroll, ink and colour on silk
works.description: Another vision of the Diamond Mountains, this time in autumn, when they are called Pungak ("maple mountain"). Temples and hermitages are tucked among the crowded peaks, with touches of red foliage. Jeong Seon travelled to Mount Geumgang several times from 1711 and painted it throughout his life.

credit.work: Overview of Inner Mount Geumgang in Autumn (Pungak naesan chongram)
credit.file: File:Jeong Seon-PungakNaesanChongramDo.jpg
credit.author: Jeong Seon

works.title: Bakyeon Falls
works.medium: Hanging scroll, ink on silk, 119.5 × 52.2 cm
works.description: A waterfall near Kaesong, counted among the "three wonders" of that old capital, crashes down a sheer cliff into a deep pool while tiny visitors watch from below. Jeong Seon exaggerated the height of the falls and darkened the cliffs with heavy ink so that the white water seems to roar out of the picture.

credit.file: File:Jeong Seon-Bakyeon pokpo.jpg
credit.author: 겸제 정선 (1676 숙종 2년 출생- 1759 영조35년 사망)

works.title: Clearing after Rain on Mount Inwang (Inwang jesaekdo)
works.medium: Hanging scroll, ink on paper, 79.2 × 138.2 cm
works.location: National Museum of Korea, Seoul (National Treasure)
works.description: Jeong Seon's masterpiece, painted at 75.
